fields.meta_title: App Landing Page Examples and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an app landing page that sends each phone to its store, gives laptops a QR code and logs every badge click by campaign.
fields.h1: Build an App Landing Page That Gets People Into the App
fields.hero_description: Describe your app and who it is for. Emergent builds the app landing page and shows each phone the right store badge, then logs every tap with the campaign behind it.
fields.features_heading: What a Mobile App Landing Page Needs
fields.features_subheading: What visitors see on the screen, and the routing behind it that gets them to the store.
fields.feature_1:
One store badge, matched to the phone

Emergent reads the visitor's device and shows the one store badge that phone can use, Apple's or Google's. Each badge opens your own listing, never a search results page.
fields.feature_2:
Screenshots set in phone frames

Upload screenshots from the current build and Emergent places them in phone frames, in the order a new user meets each screen. Captions sit under each frame in your own words.
fields.feature_3:
Every tap saved with its campaign

Each tap on a badge lands as a timestamped row with the device and the utm_campaign value. Sort the table by channel, or send new rows to HubSpot or any other tool with an API.
fields.feature_4:
A copy of the page per campaign

Ask for a version of the page for each ad set, with its own headline and hero image. All of them write to one click table, which lets you compare channels without merging exports.
fields.feature_5:
Release notes added by message

Send Emergent a message to change the headline, add notes for version 2.4 or replace a screenshot. The page updates at the same address, and saved click rows stay as they were.
fields.feature_6:
Code and click data you keep

The page and its click table export to your GitHub repository, device routing included. Run the app landing page website on Emergent under your custom domain, or host it yourself.

fields.usecase_heading: Landing Pages for Apps, by the Job They Do
fields.tab_content_1:
The App Store on an iPhone, Google Play on Android

On an iPhone, Trailmark's hiking app page shows one badge, Download on the App Store. An Android phone sees Get it on Google Play in the same spot. Each tap opens Trailmark's own listing and records the device and the campaign named in the link, such as the trail-guide email.
fields.tab_content_2:
Sign up on the page, start work in the app

Quillbook's buyers are freelancers who bill by the hour, and its web app landing page asks only for a work email and a password. Submitting creates the workspace and sends a welcome email. The visitor lands on a dashboard where sample invoice #0001 is waiting to be edited.
fields.tab_content_3:
Which ads sent this week's 1,020 store clicks

Every Monday at 9 AM, Stride Run Club's click table posts last week's campaigns to the growth channel in Slack. The newsletter turned half of its 520 visitors into store clicks. The podcast ad sent 860 visitors and only 60 clicks, and its budget went to the newsletter.
fields.tab_content_4:
When the visit starts on a laptop

Recipe blogs send Brightside Meals much of its traffic, read on laptops where a store badge leads nowhere. There the page shows a QR code that opens the right store on whichever phone scans it. An email field beside it sends the same link, and each request is saved with the blog that referred the visitor.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an App Landing Page
fields.howto_description: An app landing page has one job: get the visitor to the right store, or into the sign-up. These steps cover the copy and screenshots first, then the routing and tracking behind them.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Say what the app does in one line
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Send each device to its store
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write the headline as the job the app does for one kind of person: offline trail maps for hikers, meal plans for parents who cook after work. Put the app icon and name beside it, and keep the store badges inside the first screen.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose three or four screens a new user meets first, captured from the version that ships today. Caption each with what it lets someone do. Features planned for next quarter belong in a roadmap post, where nobody mistakes them for the current app.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Apple and Google publish badge artwork and ask that it stay unaltered: no recoloring, no redrawn logos, no translated App Store name. Link each badge to your listing in that store, and keep the Google Play badge at least as large as Apple's.
fields.howto_step_4_des: An iPhone visitor should see the App Store badge, and an Android visitor Google Play. On a laptop, neither badge helps. Show a QR code there instead, which the iPhone Camera app opens without any extra download, and print the same code on posters.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Google's guidance on intrusive interstitials warns that overlays hiding the content may hurt a page in search. For app installs it points to a small banner instead, such as Safari's Smart App Banner. Keep the page readable on the first load.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Tag every link with a campaign
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add utm_source and utm_campaign values to every link that points at the page, including the QR code on a poster. Saving the campaign with each badge click shows which channels send visitors who tap through, and which send visitors who leave.
fields.howto_step_7_des: The page counts taps on a badge, while the install itself happens in the store. Put weekly click counts beside the downloads App Store Connect reports for the same week. Plenty of clicks and few downloads points to a weak store listing.

plan.angle: The top 10 is galleries (Dribbble, Landingfolio, Lapa Ninja, One Page Love), template files (Figma, GrayGrids) and advice posts (Webflow, Adjust, Appetiser, Unbounce examples). They show what good app pages look like but stop at the screenshot: none builds the parts that decide whether a visitor reaches the store, namely the badge matched to the phone, the QR code for laptop visitors, and the click count per campaign. This page defines the term up top for the AI Overview, then shows four working app landing pages by job, each with its routing and data behind it, plus a how-to grounded in Apple, Google Play and Google Search guidance.
tab_stories: Trailmark's hiking app page reads the visitor's phone and shows one badge: the App Store on an iPhone, Google Play on Android, and each tap is logged with the campaign that sent it.
Quillbook sells an invoicing web app, so its landing page signup form creates the workspace on submit and the welcome email lands before the visitor reaches the dashboard.
Stride Run Club runs four campaigns to one app page, and the weekly table of visits and store clicks per campaign shows the podcast ad sending visitors who almost never tap a badge.
When someone opens Brightside Meals' page on a laptop, the page swaps the badges for a QR code and an email field that sends the store link to the visitor's phone.
